parallel.requirements: The run identified the program as a fixed four-point Path64 whose size is printed as 4 and noted that CLI arguments are accepted but ignored.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although the session was in swarm mode, the main actor stated no subagents were needed and retained implementation, packaging, testing, and final reporting itself.
parallel.implementation: It wrote a self-contained /output/test1.rs defining Point64, a Path64 alias as Vec<Point64>, argument collection via std::env::args, the four fixed points, and println of path.len; it also wrote Cargo.toml.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The deliverable consisted of /output/test1.rs, /output/Cargo.toml, and a compiled /output/test1 binary, all produced by the main actor with no child handoff or merge.
parallel.verification: It compiled with rustc, ran the Rust binary with no args and extra args, ran the reference executable, and diffed one reference comparison before official evaluation passed 62 of 62.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished behavior remained; the only prompt-level imperfection is that library code was kept inside test1.rs rather than a separate module, but the official evaluator accepted the solution.

serial.requirements: The run identified the same fixed-path behavior, ignored arguments, std-only Rust requirement, Cargo project requirement, and root test1.rs entry file requirement.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single serial main actor owned the whole pipeline: implement a small clipper2-like module, write the entry file, create Cargo.toml, compile, clean warnings, verify, and report.
serial.implementation: It wrote /output/clipper2.rs with Point64 and Path64, wrote /output/test1.rs that imports the module and prints path.size, then edited clipper2.rs to remove unused constructors.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial output included clipper2.rs, test1.rs, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, the compiled test1 binary, and Cargo target outputs; there was no cross-agent merge.
serial.verification: It compiled with rustc, ran the Rust binary and reference executable, then ran cargo build --release and diffed all five example inputs against the reference executable.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished or incorrect behavior remained; the warning observed after the first compile was resolved before closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized that the C++ creates a four-point path, ignores arguments, and must print 4 with a newline.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same fixed four-point path behavior and ignored-argument interface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference; both implemented enough behavior to pass every official testcase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Swarm mode was enabled, but the main actor explicitly chose direct implementation and kept all ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main actor naturally kept all implementation, packaging, warning cleanup, verification, and final-report ownership.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no real parallel decomposition; the only difference is that the parallel run declined subagent use from an available swarm-mode context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: No child brief, child result, or cross-agent interface handoff existed; the only local interface was the self-contained Point64/Path64 code in test1.rs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No cross-agent interface handoff existed; the serial run introduced a local module boundary between clipper2.rs and test1.rs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial used a clearer local module interface, while parallel kept types inline, but no inter-agent context or handoff boundary existed in either trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Implemented Point64 and Path64 directly in test1.rs, built a vector of four points, and printed path.len.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Implemented Point64 and Path64 in clipper2.rs, imported them from test1.rs, built the same path, and printed path.size.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used a smaller self-contained entry file; serial followed the module-organization requirement more literally with a separate module, but both produced equivalent observable behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; after writes and verification, the single main actor gave a final completion message.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to retrieve or join; the serial actor iterated locally from initial output to warning cleanup to final completion.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lifecycles were local and complete; serial had one extra edit-and-reverify loop, while parallel closed after the first successful implementation and checks.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The same main actor wrote test1.rs and Cargo.toml, and artifact validation found the expected entry and binary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The same main actor wrote clipper2.rs, test1.rs, and Cargo.toml, edited clipper2.rs, and artifact validation found the expected entry and binary plus Cargo outputs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had more local files and build outputs, but neither trajectory had concurrent writers, overwrites, or provenance ambiguity.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Compiled with rustc, ran several sample invocations, ran the reference executable, diffed one case, and then passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Compiled with rustc, ran the reference executable, removed a warning, ran cargo build --release, diffed all five example inputs, and then passed official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial performed broader manual example-diff verification and cargo verification; parallel performed enough checks and passed the same official suite.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The run completed normally without timeout after 71.026 agent seconds and no subagents or retries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The run completed normally without timeout after 65.827 agent seconds and no subagents or retries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run had budget pressure or incomplete closure; the serial run took slightly less agent time despite doing one extra cleanup and broader verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed evaluations under cell/status.json report solution_passed true and 62 of 62 testcases passed. The concrete process difference is organizational rather than outcome-bearing: the parallel-mode run had swarm mode available but declined to delegate and produced a self-contained test1.rs plus Cargo.toml, while the serial run produced a separate clipper2.rs module, cleaned a warning, and verified all five example argument sets. Both delivered acceptable Rust behavior for the evaluator.
parallel_contributors: The main actor kept all work local after deciding the task was trivial and no subagents were needed.
The implementation printed the four-point path length and was checked with rustc plus sample/reference comparisons.
serial_contributors: The serial actor also owned the entire solution locally and added a separate clipper2.rs module.
The serial verification included cargo build --release and diffs for all five example argument sets.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel kept Point64 and Path64 inline in test1.rs; serial used a separate clipper2.rs module.
Parallel diffed one reference argument case; serial diffed all five listed examples.
Serial observed and fixed a dead-code warning; parallel produced no logged warning-cleanup step.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; the observed differences do not explain a pass/fail gap
